actions.name: Replace a machine with a leased new title
Replace a machine with a purchased new title
Add one technician to a shift for 30 days
Preventive maintenance sweep for one manufacturer
Wayfinding and signage refresh for a zone
Comp policy pilot with control group

claims.claim: The GM's bottom 10 are driven by location, not machine quality
claims.evidence: `q1_machines.py`, `q1b.py`: bottom 10 by Σhouse_win; 9/10 are in Back Forty (M-1118 in High-Limit, retired Feb 24). Back Forty theo per machine-day is $280 vs $497 in Center Pit
claims.alternative: The machines themselves are bad: their coin-in/day is 78–128% of the Back Forty median, and none is below 75%
claims.limitation: Zone is taken from the last location in the period; only 4 moves in 6 months

claims.claim: Half of the bottom 10 are low-edge games by design
claims.evidence: `game_math.configured_rtp` = 0.95 for 5 of them; theo/day is low because theo = coin-in × 5%
claims.alternative: Players avoid them: occupancy and coin-in are at or above the zone median
claims.limitation: We cannot test changing game settings (not in the catalogue)

claims.claim: Replacing a machine in the same slot doesn't help
claims.evidence: `placements`, `machines`: M-1120 → M-5076 in B-38 on May 13; theo/day $143 → $153, both in the bottom 3
claims.alternative: The new machine needed ramp-up time: possible, but its coin-in/day already matched the zone median (106%)
claims.limitation: One swap only

claims.claim: Luck is well calibrated
claims.evidence: z = Σ(hw − theo) / √Σ(sum_bet_squared × payout_multiplier_variance); SD(z) = 1.09, mean −0.07, 1 machine with |z| > 3
claims.alternative: The variance model is wrong: an empirical SD near 1 supports it
claims.limitation: Assumes independent spins

claims.claim: M-1158 needs an inspection
claims.evidence: z = −4.57 (p ≈ 2e-6 one-sided; Bonferroni ×310 → 8e-4); hold 5.6% before Mar 10, −0.4% Mar 10–May, 6.1% in June; configured 10%. A fault repair was opened Mar 10
claims.alternative: Luck: rejected even after the multiple-test correction. A one-off jackpot: the shortfall is spread over 3 months, not one day
claims.limitation: An unusual pattern is not proof of a fault or wrongdoing

claims.claim: M-1158 runs a different payout table than recorded
claims.evidence: `hit_audit.py`: hit-rate z = (hits − p·spins)/√(p(1−p)·spins) = +124; 38.5–38.9% each month vs 31.5% configured; same-game peers 31.65%; next machine z +2.8
claims.alternative: Luck: impossible at z = 124. Meter error: payouts also exceed theo (luck z −4.6), so the tests agree. Repair-caused: the hit rate is high from January, before the Mar 10 repair
claims.limitation: Which table is actually installed is unknown until inspected; not evidence of wrongdoing

claims.claim: Back Forty demand depends on access
claims.evidence: Diff-in-diff around the W-ENT-B40 renovation closure (`floor_walkways`): Back Forty −24.6%, rest of floor +6.4%, so the diff-in-diff gap is −31.0 points
claims.alternative: Seasonality or events: the rest of the floor saw the same calendar and rose
claims.limitation: One closure; signs are a weaker intervention than a walkway

claims.claim: Downtime is small and Ridgeline-driven
claims.evidence: `operations` fault_repair: 1,207 repairs, 5,021 machine-hours, $92.6k theo lost, $213k repairs; Ridgeline 7.2 faults/machine vs Northwind 3.0, Halcyon 1.9
claims.alternative: Ridgeline sits in busier zones: it has the most faults in every zone (e.g. Center Pit 8.9 vs 2.5)
claims.limitation: Severity and parts are not observed

claims.claim: Overnight repairs wait twice as long
claims.evidence: Average wait opened → work_started: Grave 1.96 h vs Day 0.90 h, Swing 0.85 h; roster shows 1 tech on grave
claims.alternative: Fewer faults at night: there are fewer, but each waits longer
claims.limitation: Small benefit: ~1 h × 50 faults × ~$5 theo/h per month

claims.claim: The comp point price halved on May 1
claims.evidence: `loyalty_ledger` redeem: −Σpoints / Σface by day: 12.3 (Apr 30) → 5.7 (May 1), all 10 items
claims.alternative: A deliberate promotion: it isn't in `events`, and coin-in and visits did not rise (May–Jun coin-in in line with the weekday forecast)
claims.limitation: Intent unknown, so we propose a pilot, not a unilateral reversal

claims.claim: Comp cost per theo rose
claims.evidence: `property_day`: comp_cost ÷ theo 0.78% (Jan–Apr) → 0.86% (May–Jun), about $6.2k extra over 2 months. comp_cost is counted once (already inside cogs)
claims.alternative: Higher volume: the ratio normalizes by theo
claims.limitation: Small in dollars; the larger exposure is the points liability

claims.claim: Player outcomes
claims.evidence: `player_period`: wagered $163.8M, paid back $148.2M, net −$15.6M; 14.4% of player-months ahead; top 1% = 23% of theo, top 10% = 66%
claims.limitation: Carded play only; it does not match the machine meters, by design

claims.claim: The forecast beats the baseline
claims.evidence: `model2.py`: 6 candidates compared by rolling-origin CV (five 14-day folds inside Jan–Apr). Gradient boosting chosen (CV $48.2k), holdout scored once: $52.5k vs constant mean $218k, weekday mean $68.7k, ridge $54.4k. Ridge + trend: CV $50.5k but holdout $74.9k
claims.alternative: Selection bias: the test set is not used to choose. Leakage: only events announced before the cutoff
claims.limitation: The 80% conformal interval covers 75% of holdout days; two-month test

claims.claim: The forecast result is not luck, and a wider search doesn't beat it
claims.evidence: `model3.py`: 6 more candidates (multiplicative weekday × event lifts, recency weighting, recent level, richer boosting, ensembles) under the same CV protocol. CV picked an ensemble (CV $45.8k) that scored $57.5k on the holdout vs $52.5k. Paired weekly block bootstrap: MAE gap 95% CI −$1.5k to +$11.3k (not significant); baseline CI $196k–$242k, far above both
claims.alternative: Picking the best holdout model ($43.7k) would be test-set selection; we keep the model whose holdout was unseen at selection
claims.limitation: 61 holdout days; all models under-forecast May–Jun (bias ≈ −$11k/day), consistent with the June tourism dip

claims.claim: Tech vacancies slowed repairs
claims.evidence: `shift_roster` ⋈ `operations` (gaming date × shift): wait 4.9 h at 0 techs, 1.2–2.6 h at 1, 0.1–0.7 h at 2. Day shift 0.9 vs 1.7 planned in May
claims.alternative: Busier days cause both: the dose-response holds within each shift
claims.limitation: Observational; extra-tech ROI ≈ $1.2k/month vs $11.5k, so not funded

claims.claim: M-1158 is not a tampering case
claims.evidence: `deep.py` on `security_incidents`: 80 tampering-attempt reports across 67 machines, at most 3 per machine, none on M-1158
claims.limitation: Only reported incidents are recorded

claims.claim: Promotions don't pay here
claims.evidence: Residual vs weekday forecast: Locals Week (out of sample) +$16k coin-in/day ≈ +$10.6k theo over 7 days, below the $15k cost
claims.alternative: The tournament (in sample) showed +$61k, but it may coincide with other demand
claims.limitation: Two promotions observed

claims.claim: Every machine on the GM's list is profitable; a lease can't pay back in July
claims.evidence: `deep.py`: `prepared_daily_view.contribution_after_supplied_costs_usd − luck_residual_usd` (theo minus lease/service/power/repair from `cost_rules`): all 310 machines positive, the GM's 10 earn $90–$323/day. A July lease (14-day lead → 16 days) needs +$211/day of theo to repay $2,500 + 16 × $55
claims.alternative: The machines are a drag on profit: no, the minimum is +$90/day. A new title draws more play: the B-38 swap added $9/day
claims.limitation: Revenue-share lease cost depends on actual win; luck-neutral contribution approximates it with theo

claims.claim: The M-1158 anomaly appears in two independent systems
claims.evidence: `deep.py`: hit test re-run on carded `sessions` (player-tracking records, not meters): 38.6% of 461,294 spins vs 31.5%, z = +103; all others SD 1.05, max |z| 3.6
claims.alternative: Meter-reporting fault: ruled out, a separate recording system shows the same rate
claims.limitation: Carded play only (a subset of all spins)

claims.claim: A live monitor would have caught M-1158 on day one
claims.evidence: `tiger/run.py` on Tiger Cloud (TimescaleDB 2.31): cumulative hit-rate z per machine, hour by hour, over the `meter_hour` hypertable. M-1158 crosses |z| ≥ 5 after 10 hours of play (1,276 spins, $911 coin-in) on Jan 1; no other machine crosses it in 6 months (max |z| 4.08). Tiger totals match the local tables exactly
claims.alternative: Repeated testing inflates false alarms: the threshold of 5 produced none across 309 machines × ~4,300 hours
claims.limitation: Sequential testing over a longer horizon would need a formally corrected boundary (e.g. a CUSUM or alpha-spending rule)

claims.claim: Back Forty demand is foot traffic, measured directly
claims.evidence: `zone_traffic_hourly` (offline hours excluded, partial hours scaled by `coverage_minutes`): Back Forty entries −30% during the closure, Bar Row (the detour) +14%; Back Forty coin-in/machine −29%; daily elasticity of coin-in to entries 1.03 (r = 0.98)
claims.alternative: Counters broke during renovation: other zones' counters behave normally, and the detour zone rose
claims.limitation: Entries count crossings, not unique people

claims.claim: June softness follows the city, not the floor
claims.evidence: `property_day` vs each month's own weekday mix: June −4.0% (weakest); LVCVA June visitors −11.3% YoY, conventions 511k → 375k. Weekday-adjusted coin-in vs NOAA daily high: r = −0.07 (F&B −0.35)
claims.alternative: Calendar effect: weekday mix is already removed. Heat: no effect on play
claims.limitation: Six monthly points; LVCVA data was published later, so used as context only, never as a forecast input

claims.claim: The money math matches real casinos
claims.evidence: Floor hold 9.50% vs Missouri statewide slot hold 9.63% (`benchmark_state_monthly`, Jan–Jun 2025)
claims.limitation: Different market; a sanity check, not a target

claims.claim: The May 1 price cut created a +$4.1M points exposure
claims.evidence: `loyalty_ledger`: balance 156.4M points; April price 12.51 pts/$ → May–Jun 5.78; economic cost = 28% of face. Exposure if redeemed: $3.5M → $7.6M. Realized cost barely moved (313 → 335 redemptions/day)
claims.alternative: Members will never redeem: possible, so it's an exposure, not a booked cost
claims.limitation: Breakage rate unknown

claims.claim: Comps favour heavy losers, but the May change didn't
claims.evidence: `player_period` deciles of 6-month tracked net: the top 10% of losers carry 80% of tracked losses and receive 66% of comp cost. Comp/theo after May 1: heavy losers 1.39% → 1.42%, everyone else 0.92% → 1.14%
claims.limitation: Carded play only. Protective design: the pilot only restores the old price for a random half; heavy-loser visit frequency is a guardrail metric

claims.claim: Relocation can't capture unmet demand
claims.evidence: `floor_locations` + occupancy after reopening: Center Pit has 2 free slots and 45% occupancy; no zone is saturated
claims.limitation: Occupancy is a daily average; peak hours may differ
